answer: Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 284 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is cheap once and expensive in bulk. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the hollow seed, the dune timing is verifiable from the relic record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 70 keys hence pays 70 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. That is 40 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
